\overline{{{a}}}=\frac{\Delta v} {\Delta t}=\frac{+3 0 . 0 \; \mathrm{k m / h}} {2 0 . 0 \; \mathrm{s}}

2.14
 $4$ . Since the units are mixed (we have both hours and seconds for time), we need to convert everything into SI units of meters and seconds. (See Physical Quantities and Units for more guidance.)
$$
{\overline{{a}}}=\left( {\frac{+3 0 \ {\mathrm{k m / h}}} {2 0 . 0 \ {\mathrm{s}}}} \right) \left( {\frac{1 0^{3} \ {\mathrm{m}}} {1 \ {\mathrm{k m}}}} \right) \left( {\frac{1 {\mathrm{h}}} {3 6 0 0 \ {\mathrm{s}}}} \right)=0 . 4 1 7 \ {\mathrm{m / s^{2}}}
$$
2.15
Discussion
The plus sign means that acceleration is to the right. This is reasonable because the train starts from rest and ends up with a velocity to the right (also positive). So acceleration is in the same direction as the change in velocity, as is always the case.
 $\textcircled{2 8}$ EXAMPLE 2.5
Calculate Acceleration: A Subway Train Slowing Down
Now suppose that at the end of its trip, the train in Figure 2.18(a) slows to a stop from a speed of 30.0 km/h in 8.00 $\mathsf{s}$ . What is its average acceleration while stopping?
Strategy
t0, = 30.0 km/h $y$ 
 $v_{\mathrm{f}}=0$ km/h
a=? → $x$ 
FIGURE 2.20
In this case, the train is decelerating and its acceleration is negative because it is toward the left. As in the previous example, we must find the change in velocity and the change in time and then solve for acceleration.
Solution
1. Identify the knowns. $v_{0}=3 0 . 0$ kmh, $v_{\mathrm{f}}=0$ kmh trhe ri is stoped, soit velocity is O), and $\Delta t=8 . 0 0 \; \mathrm{s}$ . 2. Solve for the change in velocity, $\Delta v$ . 2.16
$$
\Delta v=v_{\mathrm{f}}-v_{0}=0-3 0 . 0 \; \mathrm{k m / h}=-3 0 . 0 \; \mathrm{k m / h}
$$
3. Plug in the knowns, $\Delta\upsilon$ and $\Delta t$ , and solve for $\bar{a}$ .
$$
\overline{{{a}}}=\frac{\Delta v} {\Delta t}=\frac{-3 0 . 0 \; \mathrm{k m / h}} {8 . 0 0 \; \mathrm{s}}
$$
2.17
4. Convert the units to meters and seconds.
$$
{\overline{{a}}}={\frac{\Delta v} {\Delta t}}=\biggr( {\frac{-3 0 . 0 \ {\mathrm{k m / h}}} {8 . 0 0 \mathrm{~ s}}} \biggr) \biggr( {\frac{1 0^{3} \mathrm{~ m}} {1 \mathrm{~ k m}}} \biggr) \biggl( {\frac{1 \mathrm{~ h}} {3 6 0 0 \mathrm{~ s}}} \biggr)=-1 . 0 4 \mathrm{~ m / s^{2}} .
$$
2.18
Discussion
The minus sign indicates that acceleration is to the left. This sign is reasonable because the train itilly has a positive velocity in this problem, and a negative acceleration would oppose the motion. Again, acceleration is in the same direction as the change in velocity, which is negative here. This acceleration can be called a deceleration because it has a direction opposite to the velocity.
